title: Sewer rat-baiting records against the wastewater payments to the pest contractor
question: Do the contractor's own treatment records keep pace with what the wastewater enterprise paid it each year?
finding: In FY2022 the feed holds 725 treatment records, against a median of 4007 in the other full years, while the Public Utilities Commission paid Agurto Corporation (Pestec) $825,549 from its wastewater operating fund, within the range of other years ($620,777 to $967,176). Empty months are common in every year; FY2022 stands out for volume, at 18% of the median year.
how: Treatment records (pyt2-uhqw) counted by fiscal year of the service date; vendor payments to AGURTO CORPORATION DBA PESTEC from department PUC and funds beginning CWP (wastewater) summed by fiscal year. The dataset does not name the contractor; it says the holder of the Citywide Integrated Pest Management contract submits it, and the City Administrator's citywide contracts with that title are held by this company.
limits: The publisher posted on 1 May 2026 that the dataset has known errors and should not be used yet; missing months may be missing uploads. The wastewater fund also pays for pest work at treatment plants and pump stations, not only sewer baiting, and payments lag the work. Records with nothing applied or eaten (8,372) are ordinary inspection visits.

sources.t: Rodent control by citywide contractor (DataSF pyt2-uhqw), Environment
